_note: The plugin's release history, newest first, shown on /changelog/. One entry per version in the manifests; `date` is the day it reached main. Groups are added, changed and fixed, each a list of plain sentences; backticks become inline code. Add the entry in the same commit that bumps the version (CI checks the newest entry matches the manifests).

changed: Updates are easier to read: one line per project with the outcome, and up to three details under it. Every voice keeps its joke on the project line and gives only a detail or two a beat of their own.
fixed: Hundreds of runs started by a script or another agent no longer flood the report; each day’s runs in a repo are one line with a count.

added: The update says what you worked on, not only what shipped. It reads what you asked in each agent session and the agent’s answer, from Claude Code, Cowork, Codex and opencode, so research, decisions and work not yet committed get a line.
It remembers your corrections. Say “shorter” or “never mention sign-ins” and it saves the preference to `style.md`, under “Learned from feedback”, and uses it next time. “Forget that” removes it.
changed: What reaches your model provider now includes short excerpts of what you asked your agents and what they answered. The privacy page and the FAQ say so.

added: A Slack markup style: bold names, identifiers in inline code and, when you ask for the numbers, one code block. Say “with Slack markup”.
A manifest for OpenAI’s plugin catalog.
changed: The Gen Z and observational voices are sharper. Both aim at the writer, the work and the industry, never at a named person.
The plugin’s logo is a PNG, so every agent’s plugin screen can show it.
fixed: The Grok install command now ends in `--trust`. Grok refuses to install without it.

added: Asking in the product’s own words: “write my standup update”, “what have we done today”. EOD and EOW still work.
Each update ends with “Try next”, three requests you have not just made.
changed: One skill, `standup`, replaces `eod-review` and `eow-review`. It writes a day, a week, a month or any range.
The title line reads “Standup EOD Tuesday, November 17th, 2026”.

added: The first public version, in one repository with the website, under MIT.
Updates for a day, a week or a month, written from git commits and the session files of eight agents.
Token counts and an estimated cost at API list prices, with models that have no listed price counted and marked unpriced.
Five voices: pirate, Gen Z, corporate, one-liner and observational.
Groups, so work, consulting and personal projects each get their own totals.
Install manifests for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and Grok.
